Local GPU will be shown as Not available when any of the following is true: * Use CPU is selected as the GPU Device in your Preferences. * No suitable GPU was found on your system. description.text: Training mode

Select this to render on the Local GPU, if available. You can select this even if no GPU is currently available on your machine. The GPU will then be used whenever the script is opened on a machine which does have a GPU available. You should also select this if you wish to render from the command line with the --gpu option. If this node requires full frames from its inputs, and is therefore unable to reduce its memory overhead, it will fall back to the CPU if an attempt to render a frame on the GPU fails due to lack of memory. When this occurs, a warning message will be printed to the console.

Enabling multi-resolution training can speed up your training by up to two times.

It does so by splitting the training into three stages - low, medium, and high resolution. During the low and medium-resolution stages, the input and ground truth images are downsized to 1/4 and 1/2 resolution respectively, allowing for fast training. In the final high-resolution stage, the model is trained on full-resolution input and ground truth images as regular CopyCat does, allowing the model to learn from the fine details and achieve optimal results. It is recommended that you disable multi-resolution training when using a large dataset of input and ground truth images (more than 100).

description.plain_text: CopyCat: Trains a neural network to replicate custom effects by feeding it before and after (or 'input' and 'ground truth') training images. Just pipe in your images, set an output directory, choose a training name and hit train. For additional control you can tweak the training parameters, and you can monitor the training progress with the contact sheet overlay and the graphs in the 'Graphs' tab.
description.text:
CopyCat: Trains a neural network to replicate custom effects by feeding it before and after (or 'input' and 'ground truth') training images. Just pipe in your images, set an output directory, choose a training name and hit train.

For additional control you can tweak the training parameters, and you can monitor the training progress with the contact sheet overlay and the graphs in the 'Graphs' tab.
